newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania CEC bank lifts deposit rates again.
newsitem.headline: Romania CEC bank lifts deposit rates again.

text.p: Romania's Casa de Economii si Consemnatiuni SA (CEC) commercial bank, formerly a savings bank, said it was increasing its term deposit rates again.
The CEC follows in the footsteps of several other Romanian commercial banks, which raised deposit rates in line with tighter monetary policies aimed at keeping inflation in rein.
"Starting March 1, the CEC will pay an annual 105 percent on individuals' term deposits, up from a previous 54 percent," a CEC statement showed on Wednesday.
Deposits at the CEC amounted to 2.6 trillion lei at the end of January, 2.1 percent up on the previous month.
This is CEC's second increase in deposit rates this year. It previously boosted one-year rates by 14 points to 54 percent.

Most banks have increased leu deposit rates since early 1997, in line with a tighter central bank monetary policy, which triggered an upswing in the one-week refinancing rate to 226.35 percent last week from 125.45 percent.
Romania's year-on-year inflation is expected to quicken to 89.5 percent this year from 56.9 percent in 1996. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 31202
